messages:
jordan (sales-eng): Hey team — starting the POC network handshake with Acme. They want Private/VPC connectivity for the trial. I sketched two options: PrivateLink (recommended) or VPC peering for Dedicated. Need infra + sec sign-off and the exact VPC/subnet details from Nate.
priya (acct-exec): @nate can you share the VPC id(s) + 3 private subnets (one per AZ) you prefer for interface endpoints? Also confirm whether your account needs an approval step for external endpoint services.
nate (acme-it): sending details shortly. one question: can we use our existing NAT/GW subnets or do endpoints need dedicated private subnets?
samir (eng-infra): Interface endpoints create ENIs in the subnets you pick — they can be private subnets where you already have outbound NAT. No special NAT requirement; just need subnet with free IPs (and 1 ENI per AZ). For PrivateLink we also need you to enable private DNS for the endpoint if you want hostnames to resolve to the VPCE.
lina (sec): Couple of security checks for Acme: 1) ensure CIDR ranges don't overlap with our endpoint ENI IPs (we'll provide ours if needed), 2) security groups must allow outbound 443 to service — we recommend limiting egress to the specific VPCE ENI IPs once created, 3) NACLs should allow ephemeral ranges for TCP 443.
samir (eng-infra): Flow for PrivateLink POC: we (Redwood) will create a VPCE service in our account and give you the service name. Customer does: aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint --vpc-id vpc-XXXX --service-name com.redwood.private.us-east-1 --vpc-endpoint-type Interface --subnet-ids subnet-AAA subnet-BBB subnet-CCC --security-group-ids sg-XXXX
jordan (sales-eng): Service name (example): com.redwood.private.us-east-1. We'll accept the endpoint once you create it (cross-account accept). After acceptance you'll see ENIs in your subnets and we can route traffic.
priya (acct-exec): If you prefer peering for Dedicated: note that peering requires non-overlapping CIDRs and route table updates on both sides. Also peering is region-limited unless you use inter-region peering. It also exposes entire routing between the two VPCs (unless you use specific route table controls).
nate (acme-it): we have 10.10.0.0/16 — ok?
lina (sec): That works. We'll avoid using 10.0.0.0/8 to keep separation. @samir can you confirm Redwood side CIDR overlap risk?
samir (eng-infra): We're good with 10.10.0.0/16. PrivateLink preferred because it keeps traffic scoped to the endpoint. For peering we'd need explicit route table entries: e.g., in your route table add a route to 172.31.0.0/16 via pcx-aaaa and in our table route back to your 10.10.0.0/16. Also disable route propagation to avoid leaking routes.
jordan (sales-eng): Quick POC suggestion: use a hosted API key for functional testing while PrivateLink/VPC set up is in flight. Hosted keys remove the network dependency so you can validate prompts/perf. We'll keep it separate from production credentials.
priya (acct-exec): Pricing note for POC: PrivateLink traffic is billed per GB on VPCE + data transfer. We'll provide an estimate after we know expected bandwidth. Peering uses standard VPC data transfer pricing.
lina (sec): Also need to track audit/logging: ensure flow logs turned on for the subnets with the endpoint and record access in Acme's SIEM. We'll want a jittered test plan (small bursts) for initial smoke tests.
samir (eng-infra): After you create the endpoint, paste the VPCE id (vpce-xxxx) here. We'll accept and then provide the target SAN for TLS (so your side can validate cert). If DNS private hostnames enabled, you should see api.redwood.internal -> VPCE resolve. Sample verify: dig +short api.redwood.internal @<your-resolver>
nate (acme-it): created endpoint vpce-0a1b2c3d in us-east-1, subnets subnet-0a, subnet-0b, subnet-0c. security group sg-07 allowing outbound 443 to 0.0.0.0/0 for now.
samir (eng-infra): Received vpce-0a1b2c3d. Accepting now. Will post acceptance event. infra-bot: VPCE request accepted: vpce-0a1b2c3d -> com.redwood.private.us-east-1 by samir (eng-infra) at 1798123490.
jordan (sales-eng): Great — once accepted, please run a curl from a host in one of the endpoint subnets: curl -v https://api.redwood.internal/v1/health -H "Authorization: Bearer <hosted-or-private-key>"
lina (sec): We'll run traffic through a test-only key and monitor TLS identity. Samir, we'll need the expected SAN and the cert fingerprint.
samir (eng-infra): SAN: api.redwood.internal, cert SHA256: ab:cd:ef:... I'll DM the full fingerprint.
priya (acct-exec): Next steps checklist for Acme: 1) confirm subnets & create VPCE, 2) enable private DNS if you want hostname mapping, 3) share VPCE id + SG rules, 4) run smoke curl with test key and share logs. We'll handle acceptance and TLS verification.
nate (acme-it): doing steps now. ETA 2 hours. thanks all :thumbsup:
priya (acct-exec): tagging this POC for billing contact—we'll only bill if bandwidth exceeds free POC threshold. Jordan will follow up on keys.
jordan (sales-eng): I'll DM a hosted test key. Once PrivateLink is green we can swap to a scoped service key for the Dedicated/Private environment. Thanks everyone.
